correctness.rationale: Twenty-one distinct edge-color pairs force k≥7 and exhaust the pairs when k=7. Each color is then incident to six edge ends and occurs on two vertices by cubicity. Two same-side vertices have a common neighbor, so a class must be a point and a nonincident line. I reconstructed the Fano blocks as translates of {0,1,3} modulo 7, verified the pair and block incidence axioms, and independently counted legal out-neighborhood assignments by enforcing exactly one arc on each unordered pair as soon as both vertices are assigned. All eight solutions have seven distinct line neighborhoods. The 168 block-preserving permutations transport one solution to all eight and exactly 21 fix it. Each partition yields 7! distinct labeled colorings, confirming 40,320 and optimality.

evidence: For the unique class take the cyclic tournament x→x+d on Z/7 for d in {1,2,4}; its neighborhoods meet once by the difference-set property (each nonzero difference occurs once). The 21 affine maps x↦ax+b with a in {1,2,4} preserve it. Conversely, the out-neighbors A of a fixed point x induce a directed 3-cycle because each a∈A has one common out-neighbor with x. Every in-neighbor b∉A∪{x} beats just one element of A, and every a∈A loses to just one such b, by regularity. Fixing A pointwise therefore fixes the in-neighbors. The stabilizer of x embeds in the three rotations of A, and the whole tournament group has order at most 7·3, hence 21.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Orbit-stabilizer under the 168 Fano point-collineations now gives exactly 168/21=8 partitions, and multiplying by 7! gives 40,320. The exact orbit, point stabilizer of the partition, and named total are all obtained from the covered unique class and its elementary symmetry. The ancillary nonincidence/collision histograms are checker data, not a distinct motivated theorem that would justify repair.

evidence: A valid f attaches each x=f(L) to the block L as its out-neighborhood N⁺(x). Propriety forbids loops, and the 21 distinct pairs give exactly one orientation per unordered pair. The Fano lines have size three and every two meet once, so this tournament is doubly regular. Conversely, the seven size-three out-neighborhoods in any order-seven doubly regular tournament are distinct and any two meet once; their 21 internal unordered pairs therefore exhaust all point pairs without duplication. They form the Fano plane. The orientation property then gives a legal nesting on that plane.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: On the fixed Fano plane this correspondence identifies tournament isomorphisms exactly with the point-collineations transporting the color partitions. Thus a classification of order-seven doubly regular tournaments is an orbit classification of the claimed optimal partitions, not just a related existence theorem.
